title: Split runtime linker and quant-kernel gatekeeper to reduce probe-time coupling
creator: Lina Chen
description: Problem: The runtime's shared-object linker path currently performs aggressive symbol resolution and opportunistic quant-kernel probing during process startup. That coupling causes probe jitter, long cold-starts, and brittle behavior when multiple CUTLASS/Triton variants are present. It also makes safe rollback and canarying of kernel bundles difficult.
goal: Introduce a thin separation layer: a deterministic runtime-linker stage that only resolves core runtime symbols, followed by an explicit Quant Kernel Gatekeeper service (in-process library) that performs compatibility checks, selective lazy-loading of quant kernels, and exposes an opt-in compatibility policy. This reduces startup jitter, enables safer kernel bundle canaries, and allows per-model kernel gating without full process reinitialization.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start median time for model launch improved by >= 20% on heterogeneous images in internal benchmark
Quant kernel probe path is executed lazily after core runtime is ready and only for models that require quant kernels
New gatekeeper emits clear telemetry: probe attempts, compatibility verdicts, fallback events, and load latencies
Canary rollout plan implemented: gatekeeper can be toggled per-host and per-pool; rollback no-op reverts without process restart
Automated unit and integration tests added; e2e perf regression suite passes on CI
risks_and_tradeoffs: Introducing an in-process gatekeeper increases code surface and requires careful memory isolation (risk: regressions under memory pressure)
Lazy-loading defers some latencies into first inference; must be mitigated via warmup/caching policies
Compatibility heuristics may need tuning across CUTLASS/Triton ABI variants; initial conservative policy may skip newer optimized kernels
Backwards compatibility: must ensure existing images without gatekeeper still work (feature-flagged rollout)
work_items: Spike: prototype splitter that performs symbol short-resolve and defers CUTLASS/Triton probe (ENG spike branch: spike/721341-runtime-split)
Design doc: outline gatekeeper API and compatibility policy (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/7234/quant-gatekeeper-design)
Implement gatekeeper: native library with deterministic probe timebox and compatibility cache
Integrate feature flag + console toggle (console-ops team) for per-pool gatekeeper opt-in
Add telemetry: Datadog dashboards and new trace spans for probe/load/fallback (dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/rw-quant-gatekeeper)
Create canary job: rollout to one dedicated pool with synthetic workloads and tokenized prompts
Post-deploy: run regression perf harness and compare against baseline traces (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3921)
Docs: update ops runbook for kernel bundle rollbacks and emergency toggles
implementation_notes: We will build the gatekeeper as a separate shared object (librw_gatekeeper.so) loaded by the runtime after core linker init. The gatekeeper will use a deterministic probe scheduler (max 50ms per probe attempt, exponential backoff) and a signed kernel manifest to decide compatibility. Kernel manifests will be published alongside cutlass/triton bundles and validated with existing artifact signatures. The runtime loader will expose an explicit API: register_model_kernels(model_id, manifest_uri) and request_kernel_for_op(op_signature).
benchmarks_and_metrics: Baseline: model-launch cold-start median = 180ms (heterogeneous CI image)

notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing CUTLASS/Triton ABI surfaces. The gatekeeper is a compatibility shim that only affects probe/loading timing and decisioning; any kernel code remains untouched. The feature is behind a feature flag and has a no-op fallback to preserve existing behavior if disabled.
